Extract Pathways from Higher-Order Network Objects

Source: R/pathways.R
pathways.Rd

pathways() turns a higher-order result into pathway strings in arrow notation, "A B -> C": the states before the arrow lead, together, to the state after it. The strings are what cograph::plot_simplicial() draws, one simplex per pathway. Which pathways are returned depends on the input:

  • a net_hon gives its higher-order edges, those whose source node has order above 1, i.e. the transitions that differ from a first-order Markov chain, ranked by count;

  • a net_hypa gives its anomalous paths, over- or under-represented relative to the hypergeometric null model, the over-represented ones first;

  • a net_mogen gives every transition at the optimal order (or the order given), ranked by count;

  • a netobject built from sequences is first turned into a HON or a HYPA, and that result's pathways are returned;

  • a net_association_rules gives its rules {A, B} => {C} as "A B -> C": antecedent items become the sources, consequent items the target. Rules whose antecedent and consequent together hold the same items describe the same simplex, so only the highest-lift rule per item set is kept; the rules are ranked by lift, then confidence;

  • a net_link_prediction gives its predicted links, ranked by score; with evidence = TRUE each predicted edge A -> B is extended with the common neighbours that support it, "A cn1 cn2 -> B".

The strings keep only which pathways passed the filters, not the counts, probabilities, scores or tests behind them; those stay in the source object (for a MOGen, mogen_transitions() gives them per order).

Usage

pathways(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_hon'
pathways(x, min_count = 1L, min_prob = 0, top = NULL, order = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypa'
pathways(x, type = "all", ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
pathways(x, ho_method = c("hon", "hypa"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_association_rules'
pathways(x, top = NULL, min_lift = NULL, min_confidence = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_link_prediction'
pathways(x, method = NULL, top = 10L, evidence = TRUE, max_evidence = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mogen'
pathways(x, order = NULL, min_count = 1L, min_prob = 0, top = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

The object to read: a net_hon, net_hypa or net_mogen (from build_hon(), build_hypa() or build_mogen()), a netobject built from sequences, a net_association_rules (from association_rules()) or a net_link_prediction (from predict_links()). A netobject of an association method (whose rows are variables) or a one-hot netobject raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input; a network without its sequences stops pathways().

...

For the netobject method: passed to the pathways() method of the HON or HYPA built from it, so min_count, min_prob, top and order apply to a HON and type to a HYPA. Ignored by the other methods.

min_count

For a HON or a MOGen: the smallest transition count kept, which filters out rare observations. Default 1 (all).

min_prob

For a HON or a MOGen: the smallest transition probability kept. Default 0 (all).

top

How many pathways to keep after ranking: by count for a HON or a MOGen, by lift then confidence for association rules (after the item sets are de-duplicated), and by score for link predictions. Default NULL (all), except for link predictions, whose default is 10. Not used for a HYPA.

order

For a HON: keep only pathways whose source has this order. Default NULL, every order above 1; order 1 returns nothing. For a MOGen: the Markov order to extract. Default NULL, the optimal order from model selection; an order below 1 returns character(0).

type

For a HYPA: which anomalies to include, "all" (default), "over" (over-represented paths) or "under" (under-represented ones).

ho_method

For a netobject: the higher-order model built from its sequences, "hon" (default, build_hon()) or "hypa" (build_hypa()), each with its default settings. The network must carry the sequences it was built from.

min_lift

For association rules: the smallest lift kept, on top of the threshold the rules were mined with. Default NULL (no further filter).

min_confidence

For association rules: the smallest confidence kept, on top of the mining threshold. Default NULL (no further filter).

method

For link predictions: the prediction method whose links are returned. Default NULL, the first method in the object. A method the object does not hold returns character(0).

evidence

For link predictions: whether to extend each predicted link A -> B with its common neighbours, the nodes with an edge from A and an edge to B, giving "A cn1 cn2 -> B". Default TRUE. Without a stored adjacency matrix the links are returned as "A -> B".

max_evidence

For link predictions with evidence = TRUE: the most common neighbours added to one link; when there are more, those with the largest summed weight of the edges from A and to B are kept. Default 3.

Value

A character vector of pathway strings in arrow notation (e.g. "A B -> C"), one per pathway and in the ranking order described above, ready for cograph::plot_simplicial(). Every method returns this shape, and character(0) when nothing passes its filters.

Methods (by class)

  • pathways(net_hon): Higher-order edges of a HON.

  • pathways(net_hypa): Anomalous paths of a HYPA.

  • pathways(netobject): Higher-order pathways of a network's sequences.

  • pathways(net_association_rules): Association rules as pathways.

  • pathways(net_link_prediction): Predicted links as pathways.

  • pathways(net_mogen): Transitions of a MOGen at one order.

Examples

# \donttest{
seqs <- list(c("A","B","C","D"), c("A","B","C","A"))
hon <- build_hon(seqs, max_order = 3)
pw <- pathways(hon)
# }

trans <- list(c("A","B","C"), c("A","B"), c("B","C","D"), c("A","C","D"))
rules <- association_rules(trans, min_support = 0.3, min_confidence = 0.3,
                           min_lift = 0)
pathways(rules)
#> [1] "D -> C" "A -> B" "A -> C" "B -> C"

seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:5], 50, TRUE),
  V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:5], 50, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:5], 50, TRUE)
)
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
pred <- predict_links(net, methods = "common_neighbors")
pathways(pred)
#> [1] "C A B D -> E"
